html:
A revolt against the Tang dynasty in China, launched in 755 by the general An Lushan and fought until 763. It was among the most destructive wars of its age and ended the Tang golden age.

An Lushan, a frontier commander of Sogdian and Turkic descent, had won the favour of Emperor Xuanzong and command of huge armies in the north. In late 755 he marched south, and in 756 his troops took Chang'an. The emperor fled to Sichuan, and on the way his guards forced the death of his beloved consort Yang Guifei. Xuanzong gave up the throne.

An Lushan was murdered by his son in 757, and his general Shi Siming carried on the war. The Tang won only with the help of troops from the Uyghur Khaganate.

The cost was huge. Registered population fell by tens of millions, though partly because records broke down. Afterwards regional military governors ran their provinces almost freely, the Tibetans seized the western lands, and the Tang never fully recovered. The poet Du Fu lived through it and wrote about it.
sum: A revolt against the Tang dynasty in China, launched in 755 by the general An Lushan and fought until 763. It was among the most destructive wars of its age and ended the Tang golden age.
